# Translation of Iliad Book 19, lines 184-201

Then in turn, Agamemnon, lord of men, addressed him:

"I rejoice, son of Laertes, having heard your speech;
for you have set forth all things in proper order and explained them.
These things I am willing to swear to, and my heart urges me,
nor will I break my oath before the gods. But let Achilles
remain here, eager though he is for the god of war;
and let all the rest of you remain gathered together, until the gifts
come from my tent and we make trustworthy oaths.
And to you myself I give this command and order:
Select the best young men from all the Achaeans
to carry the gifts from my ship—all those we promised
yesterday to give to Achilles—and to bring the women.
And let Talthybius quickly throughout the broad army of the Achaeans
prepare a boar to be sacrificed to Zeus and Helios the Sun."

---

**Note:** This passage is from Homer's *Iliad*, Book 19. Odysseus (Laertiad) has just spoken, and Agamemnon responds, agreeing to fulfill his oath to Achilles by providing the promised gifts and compensation.
